docs.title: Translating the HiCarta manual
docs.text: The manual (docs/) is bilingual, built with MkDocs Material and the mkdocs-static-i18n plugin.

docs.title: How it is organized
docs.text:
docs/
  images/        shared screenshots (language-neutral)
  ja/            Japanese — the SOURCE you edit by hand
  en/            English  — GENERATED from ja/ (default language, site root /)
  • Every page exists once per language at the same relative path, e.g. docs/ja/usage.md ↔ docs/en/usage.md.
  • English is the default and is served at the site root (/); Japanese is at /ja/. A language switcher appears in the top-right of the header.
  • Images live in docs/images/ and are shared. Reference them from a page as ../images/overview.png.

docs.title: Editing workflow
docs.text:
1. Edit the Japanese page under docs/ja/ (this is the source of truth).
  2. Ask Claude to update the matching English page under docs/en/ from the Japanese version — same relative path. For example: "Update the English usage page (docs/en/usage.md) to match the Japanese one."
  3. Commit and push. The GitHub Action rebuilds and publishes the site.

Keep the two files structurally parallel (same headings, tables, links, and code blocks) so the switcher lands the reader on the equivalent section. Do not translate file names, paths, commands, or code — only prose and headings.

docs.title: Adding a new page
docs.text:
1. Create docs/ja/<name>.md and docs/en/<name>.md.
  2. Add it to nav: in mkdocs.yml using the unprefixed path (- New page: <name>.md).
  3. Add the Japanese label under the ja locale's nav_translations: in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Build locally (optional)
docs.text:
pip install mkdocs-material mkdocs-static-i18n
mkdocs serve      # preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build      # one-off build into site/

If a translation is missing, the plugin falls back to the default language (English), so the site never breaks mid-translation.

docs.title: HiCarta
docs.text:
Explore Hi-C maps as easily as online maps.

HiCarta is a free desktop application for interactive visualization of Hi-C data. Pan and zoom with simple drag and scroll gestures, from a whole-genome view down to individual genes. View loops, ChIP-seq signals, and other genomic tracks alongside Hi-C maps, compare maps across experimental conditions, create custom tracks in R, and export editable figures for publication.

HiCarta runs on your own computer without requiring a separate server. Once R is installed, you can launch HiCarta with a double-click. The name "Carta" alludes to maps and charts.

Watch the 4-minute demo above or the 1-minute overview.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Hi-C map Two conditions in a split view (upper right and lower left) Rotated map + loops + ChIP-seq ChIP-seq tracks + genes Custom track written in R Multiple chromosomes in a single view

All the figures above were exported from HiCarta as PDFs. Learn more in What HiCarta can do.

docs.title: Work with your existing data files
docs.text: Open .hic files and track data from your own computer, a web server, Dropbox shared links or Amazon S3 (public or private). HiCarta retrieves only the required portions of remote .hic and bigWig files by default, so you do not need to download entire files in advance. How HiCarta works explains how this works.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Install R (4.1 or later) from https://cran.r-project.org.

  2. On GitHub, download the code using Code → Download ZIP and unzip it.

  3. Start HiCarta.

    • Windows — double-click run_windows.bat.
    • macOS — double-click run_mac.command (if it is blocked, right-click → Open).

    On the first launch, the required R packages are installed automatically, which can take a few minutes. 4. HiCarta appears in your web browser. Next, open the demo data in First 5 minutes.

See Installation and Setup details & troubleshooting for details.

Developer: Hideki Tanizawa (rafysta@gmail.com), Institute for Genetic Medicine, Hokkaido University Source: github.com/rafysta/HiCarta · MIT License Please submit questions, bug reports, and feature requests through GitHub Issues.

docs.title: Comparison with other tools
docs.text: Each Hi-C visualization tool has its own strengths. HiCarta focuses on browsing and comparing your lab’s data locally and exporting the results as figures for publication. Other tools may be better suited to exploring public datasets or building large collaborative data portals.

docs.title: What HiCarta is good for
docs.text:
• Viewing your lab's Hi-C data on your own computer, without setting up a server.
  • Quickly comparing Hi-C maps from two conditions at the same genomic region.
  • Exporting the current view as an editable figure for publication.
  • Visualizing custom analysis results in R alongside the Hi-C map.
  • Managing hundreds of samples in Excel and sharing a common data catalog with collaborators.
  • Sharing unpublished data only with collaborators who have been granted access.

docs.title: What other tools are good for
docs.text:
• Browsing a wide range of public data — 3D Genome Browser, WashU Epigenome Browser, UCSC Genome Browser and HiGlass (higlass.io) host many public datasets.
  • Sharing a view via a URL — Juicebox Web and HiGlass can share the current view as a URL.
  • Comparing two genomes side by side — use the linear synteny view of JBrowse 2.
  • Generating multiple figures with a consistent layout using scripts — pyGenomeTracks and plotgardener are well suited to this task.

docs.title: Data catalog (.xlsx)
docs.text:
In HiCarta, contact maps and tracks can be opened from a data catalog: an Excel file (.xlsx) with one row per sample. You can also open a file by entering its path or URL directly, without a catalog. Open the Data browser using the Data button at the top of the screen and load the catalog. It appears as a searchable, filterable sample list. Clicking a row displays the sample details and the actions available for its file type (open as a contact map, open as a comparison, add as a track, or open in IGV).

A reusable template is included in the repository: HiCarta_catalog_template.xlsx.

The catalog can be stored on a local drive, a network drive, or at a URL (e.g., an .xlsx file shared over HTTP). HiCarta reloads the catalog each time you click Load catalog, so updates to the shared file can be retrieved on the next load. Google Sheets is not supported directly; export the spreadsheet as an .xlsx file before sharing it.

docs.title: Required
docs.text: Column Meaning id A numeric identifier used in the sample list and ID search. Unique IDs are recommended but not required. Duplicate IDs generate a warning but do not exclude rows (HiCarta does not use IDs internally as row keys). This allows sample sets with independent numbering schemes to be combined in one catalog. name Sample name shown in the list. path File path or URL. Can hold several ;-separated entries (see below).

docs.title: Recommended (recognized by HiCarta)
docs.text: Column Meaning file_type hic / bigwig / bed / gff3 / bs. If empty, inferred from the file extension. experiment_type Experiment type (e.g., Hi-C, ChIP-seq, or RNA-seq); available as a filter. project Project name; becomes a filter. sample_sheet Sample sheet or batch identifier; becomes a filter. date YYYY-MM-DD (recommended). Also accepted: YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY.MM.DD, YYYYMMDD, native Excel dates. Supports date-range filtering. genome Genome/assembly name. label Display label for each ;-separated entry in path (one label per entry or a single shared label). comment Free text; included in the search across all columns.

docs.title: Settings columns (set_ prefix)
docs.text:
Columns whose names start with set_ are per-sample defaults applied when the sample is opened. They never appear in the list or the filters.

Column Effect when the sample is opened set_norm Normalization to select (e.g. ICE, KR, NONE). If unspecified, HiCarta automatically selects the first available option in this order: ICE → KR → Raw. set_vmax Initial color-scale maximum. set_resolution Fix the display resolution (bp) instead of adjusting it automatically as you zoom. set_color Default track color (track types). set_height Default track height in pixels (track types).

docs.title: Your own columns
docs.text: Additional columns are retained and shown in the detail view. A column with at most 20 distinct values automatically becomes a dropdown filter in the sidebar. For example, add a tissue or condition column to filter by that metadata.

docs.title: Multiple files in one row (;)
docs.text:
path, label and every set_ column may hold several values separated by ; (the full-width ； also works). Within a row, each of these columns must contain either one value (shared by all entries) or exactly as many values as there are entries in path.

Two uses:

  • A track set — several bigWigs belonging to one sample; "Add as track" lets you select the entry to add.
  • A virtual multi-resolution dataset — several single-resolution .hic files of the same sample in one row. Opening the row with “auto” treats them as one dataset: HiCarta switches between the files as you zoom and adjusts their signal intensity for consistent display. This provides compatibility with legacy files stored separately by resolution; for new datasets, a single multi-resolution .hic file is recommended.

Note

In auto mode only the normalizations present in every file are offered in Display → Map → Normalization. Open a single entry to use that file's own normalizations.

docs.title: Directive rows: #show
docs.text: A row with #show in the id cell is a directive rather than a data row. Enter any marker (e.g., 1) in the columns that should be visible in the list initially. Viewers can still toggle columns with the Columns button; id and name are always shown. Rows whose id starts with # but is not a known directive are ignored with a warning.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
When a catalog is loaded, invalid rows — a missing or non-numeric id, an empty path, mismatched ; counts — are excluded. Other issues (a duplicate id, a path that looks like neither a file nor a URL, an invalid date, an unknown file_type or set_ column) are warnings only; the row still loads.

A path is considered well-formed if it has a URL scheme (e.g., https://), a path separator (/ or \), or a file extension. A value with none of those (ICE, KR, 5000) may indicate a misaligned column, so it is flagged — and opening such a row stops with the same explanation instead of failing later with a message about the file.

Only the counts appear above the table, one per line — "Excluded rows: 3 (click to see them)". Click a line to expand the list of sample names and the corresponding reasons; click again to collapse it. When there are many, the list stops at the first 200 and the rest are summarized as "...and N more".

docs.title: Bookmarks as Excel
docs.text:
Bookmarks (Navigate panel) record only the genomic location — the chromosome and the X / Y ranges. Clicking a bookmark navigates to the same region in the currently open dataset, making bookmarks useful for comparisons across samples. Two buttons allow bookmarks to be exchanged as an .xlsx file:

  • Save to Excel downloads the current list (one row per bookmark; columns bookmark_name, chr, start, end, chr_y, ystart, yend, comment).
  • Load from Excel (append) reads such a file and appends its rows to the current list — existing bookmarks are never touched. Invalid rows are skipped and reported with the name and reason, like the catalog itself. Files saved by older versions that contain catalog_id / path / norm and the other display columns still load — those columns are ignored.

The file is a standard Excel workbook, so you can annotate the comment column, curate a list of regions by hand, or share it with collaborators.

docs.title: Private data on Amazon S3
docs.text:
In addition to public URLs, path can specify an Amazon S3 object using s3://bucket/key (e.g. s3://uo-cgf/P/020/NAME/NAME.hic). This works for every file type (.hic, bigWig, BED, …), and the catalog itself can also be stored on S3.

  • Public files are read without credentials, whether specified as an https://….amazonaws.com/… URL or as s3://.
  • Files that are not public are read with an AWS access key stored on your computer, which HiCarta uses to sign the request. Access is determined by the permissions configured in S3 (e.g., for a lab or P01 group). If you lack permission, HiCarta displays an error message.
  • If a file written as an https:// S3 URL is later made private, the same URL keeps working for anyone who has the required access permission.

Store the credentials in the same file used by the AWS CLI:

# Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.aws\credentials   Mac: ~/.aws/credentials
[hicarta]
aws_access_key_id     = AKIA...
aws_secret_access_key = ...

Enter hicarta as the AWS profile under Setting → Edit config file… and save (empty = [default]). The dialog indicates whether credentials were found. The access key itself is not stored in config.txt. The region is detected automatically.

docs.title: Open in IGV
docs.text: For track rows, the detail view offers Open in IGV: the file (and the region currently in view) is sent to a running instance of IGV Desktop through IGV's remote port. HiCarta does not launch IGV automatically. Start IGV and enable its remote port: View → Preferences → Advanced → “Enable port” (default 60151). Optionally set igv_genome in config.txt (or Setting → Edit config file…) to also tell IGV which genome to load.

docs.title: Converting old files
docs.text:
The scripts/ directory contains four standalone converters between the catalog and two legacy formats (Juicer-style menu, IGV track-list XML):

Rscript scripts/juicer_menu_to_catalog.R  menu.txt     catalog.xlsx [--collapse]
Rscript scripts/igv_xml_to_catalog.R      tracks.xml   catalog.xlsx
Rscript scripts/catalog_to_juicer_menu.R  catalog.xlsx menu.txt
Rscript scripts/catalog_to_igv_xml.R      catalog.xlsx tracks.xml

--collapse additionally rewrites legacy per-normalization names (NAME_ICE.5kb.hic → NAME.hic) and removes duplicates — useful after regenerating data as single multi-resolution .hic files. See scripts/README.md.

docs.title: Data formats
docs.text: HiCarta supports several genomic data formats. Contact maps use .hic files; signals, genomic intervals, gene annotations, loops, and other data are displayed as tracks.

docs.title: Contact maps: .hic (Juicer)
docs.text:
This is the primary contact map format. HiCarta supports random access to genomic regions at multiple resolutions. By default, remote .hic files are streamed using HTTP range requests. .hic files are opened from the data catalog or by entering the path directly (Data → Direct file).

  • Chromosome names must match those in the .hic file (e.g. I / II / III for S. pombe).
  • A .hic file may contain only one resolution. HiCarta adjusts the requested resolution and normalization to those available in the file. Several single‑resolution files for the same sample can be registered in one catalog row and be opened together as a virtual multi‑resolution dataset.

docs.title: Tracks
docs.text: Format Panel type Notes bigWig bigWig quantitative signal, drawn as a filled area BED BED intervals, drawn as boxes GFF3 gene (GFF3) gene models; parsed once and cached as <gff3>.genes.rds *_BS.txt Border Strength TAD boundary strength; see below

docs.title: Border Strength (*_BS.txt)
docs.text:
This format is produced by BorderStrength. Columns: chr, start, end, BS, BS.norm, boundary, TADid, TAD (200 bp bins). HiCarta plots BS.norm as an area (positive red, negative blue, baseline 0) with dashed lines at positions where boundary != 0.

A header containing these column names is expected. Files without a header are interpreted by column position (chr, start, end, BS, BS.norm, ...). Bin sizes are not restricted to 200 bp; other sizes, such as 40 kb, are also supported.

docs.title: hic200‑cpp raw maps (.txt.gz) → .hic
docs.text: hic200‑cpp outputs a gzip-compressed text representation of a contact matrix (bin1 bin2 score, upper triangle, 200 bp global bin indices). Rather than reading the large text file directly, convert it once to a compressed, indexed, multi-resolution .hic file and load it locally. The resulting file is typically comparable in size to the .txt.gz file but supports much faster regional access.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Java (to run Juicer Tools)
  • juicer_tools.jar — https://github.com/aidenlab/juicer/wiki/Download
  • the matching bin definition file (e.g. sample/bin_def_200bp.txt), which maps each global bin index to (chromosome, start)

docs.title: Conversion outline
docs.text:
The repository includes a wrapper script that automates the conversion:

JUICER=/path/to/juicer_tools.jar \
  bash scripts/convert_hic200_to_hic.sh sample/bin_def_200bp.txt file1.txt.gz [file2.txt.gz ...]

The script generates a corresponding .hic file (e.g., file1.hic) alongside each input file. Configure the conversion using the following environment variables: RES (resolutions), JMEM (Java heap), JUICER (path to the jar).

Internally, the script (1) derives chrom.sizes from the bin definition, (2) maps each 200 bp bin index to its midpoint, (3) writes Juicer "short with score" records (<str1> <chr1> <pos1> <frag1> <str2> <chr2> <pos2> <frag2> <score>), and (4) runs juicer_tools pre -n (no normalization) to build the multi‑resolution .hic.

After conversion, register the new .hic in your data catalog and open it from the Data browser. See also scripts/README.md.

docs.title: Demo data
docs.text: To help you get started, we provide a demo catalog containing only publicly available data. All listed files are available online. By default, HiCarta retrieves only the required portions of .hic and bigWig files; other formats are read in full when needed.

docs.title: Opening the demo catalog
docs.text:
In Data → Data browser, paste the following URL into the catalog field and click Load catalog.

https://uo-cgf.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/HiCarta/demo/HiCarta_demo_catalog.xlsx

The same catalog is included in the repository at sample/HiCarta_demo_catalog.xlsx (select it with Browse…). See First 5 minutes for step-by-step instructions.

docs.title: Proliferating and senescent IMR90 cells (id 2, 3, 11–16)
docs.text:
Iwasaki O, Tanizawa H, Kim KD et al. Involvement of condensin in cellular senescence through gene regulation and compartmental reorganization. Nat Commun 10, 5688 (2019). GEO GSE118494

  • Hi-C (id 2, 3) — Generated exclusively from samples deposited in GEO. The proliferating-cell (Growing) map combines two samples (GSM3330966, GSM3330967), and the oncogene-induced senescent-cell (OIS, H-RasV12) map combines three samples (GSM3330968–GSM3330970). Resolutions range from 5 kb to 1 Mb, with KR-normalized and unnormalized (NONE) data available.
  • ChIP-seq (id 11–16) — identical to the supplementary bigWig files in GEO. Copies of the same files are hosted on Amazon S3 to facilitate reliable partial reads in HiCarta.

docs.title: High-depth Hi-C and chromatin loops in IMR90 cells (id 1, 21, 41)
docs.text:
Rao SSP, Huntley MH, Durand NC et al. A 3D map of the human genome at kilobase resolution reveals principles of chromatin looping. Cell 159, 1665–1680 (2014). GEO GSE63525

  • Hi-C (id 1) — A .hic file combining in situ Hi-C data from IMR90 cells (seven libraries). Resolutions range from 5 kb to 500 kb, with KR normalization. These data are suitable for detailed visualization of kilobase-scale regions and loops.
  • Loops (id 21) — GSE63525_IMR90_HiCCUPS_looplist.txt.gz from GEO (8,040 loops detected by HiCCUPS), with chr added to the chromosome names. The observed contact count (column o) is used as the loop strength. The processed file is available at sample/IMR90_loops_Rao2014_HiCCUPS_hg19.bedpe.

docs.text:

Hi-C data were collected from synchronized cdc25-22 cells 20 minutes (G2) and 50 minutes (mitosis) after release from the block.
