docs.text:
• Human — protein-coding genes of GENCODE v19 (hg19), with one representative transcript per gene.
  • Fission yeast — PomBase gene models (sample/Schizosaccharomyces_pombe_all_chromosomes.gff3).

docs.title: Bookmarks
docs.text: sample/HiCarta_demo_bookmarks_hg19.xlsx contains bookmarks (hg19) for the two demo regions (chr5) and for 14 senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) genes. Load it with Load from Excel (append) in the bookmark section of the Navigate panel.

docs.title: Using the data
docs.text: If you use the demo data in a paper or elsewhere, please cite the original publication for each dataset. To cite HiCarta itself, see the citation instructions in the README.

docs.title: What HiCarta can do
docs.text: Explore HiCarta’s features through screenshots and short videos. Each feature links to the relevant sections of Usage and Screens & controls for detailed instructions. All examples on this page use publicly available demo data visualized in HiCarta.

docs.title: Navigate Hi-C maps intuitively
docs.text:
Drag to pan and scroll to zoom in and out. The resolution adjusts automatically to the zoom level, allowing seamless navigation from an entire chromosome down to a few kilobases. HiCarta retrieves only the data needed to render the current view, helping maintain responsive navigation even with high-resolution maps and large genomes.

  • Go anywhere — enter a chromosome and a range to move to the region you want. → Move to any location
  • Move with buttons — pan the map in fixed increments using the eight directional buttons. → Move with buttons
  • Bookmarks — save a named region of interest and return to it with one click. A bookmark records only the genomic position, so after switching samples the same bookmark shows the same region in the new sample. Bookmarks can also be exchanged as Excel files. → Bookmark a region of interest

docs.title: Explore whole-genome and inter-chromosomal contacts
docs.text: Display all chromosomes along both axes to visualize every chromosome pair at once, then zoom into any block. You can also choose a different chromosome for the vertical axis to show only the contacts between two chromosomes (trans). → Navigate

docs.title: Compare Hi-C maps from different conditions
docs.text:
Open a second sample to compare Hi-C maps from different conditions on one screen. There are three ways to compare:

View What it does Split Shows sample A above and sample B below the diagonal (upper right and lower left). Curtain Drag the divider to switch between the samples on its two sides. The spacebar switches the whole map between A and B instantly. Difference Shows the log2 ratio or the difference of the two maps on a symmetric scale centered on 0. Palettes designed for users with color vision deficiencies are available.

When automatic sequencing-depth correction is enabled, HiCarta scales sample B using the ratio of total contact counts (A / B). → Tutorial: compare two conditions

docs.title: View Hi-C maps alongside other genomic data
docs.text:
The following tracks can be shown below the Hi-C map. Tracks remain synchronized with the Hi-C map as you navigate, keeping the displayed data aligned to the same genomic region.

Track What it shows Rotated map (RotMap) The Hi-C map as a triangular track rotated by 45 degrees. Configure the distance range, orientation, colors, normalization, and observed/expected (O/E) display. Loops (arcs) BEDPE files, HiCCUPS loop lists and ChIA-PET / HiChIP tables, drawn as arcs. Color and line width can reflect interaction strength. Signal bigWig (e.g., ChIP-seq signals). The drawing resolution can be set for each track. Genomic intervals and genes BED, GFF3 Domain boundary strength Border Strength (*_BS.txt)

  • Tracks only — hide the square contact map and display only the rotated map and other tracks. You can also show tracks without opening a Hi-C map at all. → Tracks without a contact map
  • Appearance — set the name, color, height and maximum / minimum of each track. Drag the chips to change the order. → Tracks

docs.title: Manage your samples with a single Excel file
docs.text: No database is required. Create an Excel data catalog with one row per sample. Add metadata columns, such as cell type, experimental condition, or antibody. Columns with 20 or fewer distinct values become filters, helping you find the desired data among hundreds of samples. Share the same Excel file with collaborators to work from a common catalog. → Data catalog

docs.title: Share unpublished data securely
docs.text: Assign access-control tags to files stored in Amazon S3 and configure permissions based on those tags so that only authorized users can open the files. Once the permissions are configured, you can expand access (e.g., upon publication) by changing the relevant tag. There is no need to move the files or change the paths in your Excel catalog. → Private data on Amazon S3

docs.title: Create custom tracks in R (plugins)
docs.text: Extend HiCarta’s built-in visualization features by creating custom tracks in R. A typical plugin is a single R script defining read() and draw() functions. Place it in the plugins/ folder to make it available as a new track type. HiCarta automatically generates a settings dialog for the plugin. Plugins also work with the catalog, with saving and restoring sessions, and with figure export. Two plugins are included: one draws a table with the columns chr, start, end and value, and one draws a Virtual 4C profile read from a .hic file. → Plugins

docs.title: Export editable, publication-ready figures
docs.text: Use the print preview to review the figure while adjusting its contents, including coordinate ticks, the legend, tracks, and sample information. In the PDF, the Hi-C map is saved as a raster image and the axes, labels and tracks as editable vector graphics. This helps keep file sizes manageable while allowing further editing in Illustrator, Inkscape, or similar tools. PNG output and printing directly to a printer are also available. → Tutorial: make a publication figure

docs.title: Work with your existing data files
docs.text:
Open .hic files and track data from your own computer, a web server, Dropbox shared links or Amazon S3 (public or private).

  • On-demand data retrieval — by default, HiCarta retrieves only the portions of remote .hic and bigWig files required for the current view with HTTP range requests. There is no need to download the whole file.
  • Caching for faster navigation — previously retrieved data are cached in memory, speeding up revisits to cached regions.
  • On a slow connection — a setting switches to a mode that saves the whole file locally before drawing (hic_engine = download).
  • BED, GFF3 and Border Strength files are read in full when loaded.

→ How HiCarta works

docs.title: Other features
docs.text:
• Color scale — choose from four palettes (matlab, gentle, red, blue) and set the maximum with a linear or log10 slider. → Change the contrast (color intensity)

  • Normalization and resolution — switch the normalization (KR, ICE, Raw and so on) and the resolution of an open map without reopening it. → Display

  • Sessions — save the whole view, including data sources, the genomic region, the color scale, and all tracks, to one file (.json), and restore it later. → Save the view and reproduce it later (session)
  • Open in IGV — send a sample from the catalog to a running IGV. → Open in IGV
  • Interface language — switch the interface between English and Japanese. → Switch the display language

docs.title: First 5 minutes
docs.text:
Learn the basic operations of HiCarta using the demo catalog, a collection of publicly available datasets. There are six steps: load the catalog → open a Hi-C map → move and zoom → add tracks → move with bookmarks → export a figure.

All data are available online, so no manual downloads are required. By default, HiCarta retrieves only the portions of each .hic or bigWig file needed for the current view.

Before you start

Install and start HiCarta (Installation). An internet connection is required.

docs.title: 1. Load the demo catalog
docs.text:
1. Click Data at the top of the screen.

  2. On the Data browser tab, paste the following URL into the "Catalog (.xlsx) path or URL" field.

    https://uo-cgf.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/HiCarta/demo/HiCarta_demo_catalog.xlsx

  3. Click Load catalog.

The sample list appears. Use the filters on the left to narrow the list by columns such as organism (organism) and experiment type (experiment_type). See Demo data for a list of available datasets.

docs.title: 2. Open a Hi-C map
docs.text:
1. Click the row IMR90 Hi-C, deep (Rao 2014) in the list.
  2. In the details that appear, click Open as contact map.

The high-depth Hi-C map of human IMR90 cells (Rao et al., 2014) opens.

docs.title: 3. Move and zoom
docs.text:
• Drag to pan and use the mouse wheel to zoom in and out. The resolution changes automatically with the zoom.
  • To go straight to a region, choose chr5 as the X-axis chromosome in the Navigate panel on the left, enter 147500000 as the start and 150500000 as the end, and click Go to region.
  • If the map is too light or too dark, adjust Max value under Display → Map.

In this region, the map shows punctate contact enrichments corresponding to loops.

docs.title: 4. Add tracks
docs.text:
Return to the Data browser by clicking Data. Select each of the following rows in turn, then click Add as track. Before adding a track, you can adjust its label, color, and height.

Row What it shows IMR90 loops (Rao 2014, HiCCUPS) Loops drawn as arcs CTCF ChIP-seq Growing CTCF ChIP-seq signal SMC1 ChIP-seq Growing ChIP-seq signal of SMC1, a subunit of cohesin Genes (GENCODE v19, protein-coding) Genes

In addition, click Add as rotated map in the row IMR90 Hi-C, deep (Rao 2014) to show the Hi-C map as a triangular track rotated by 45 degrees. All tracks remain aligned with the Hi-C map as you navigate.

Tips for improving visibility

  • Click a track's name under Display → Tracks to change its settings. Setting the maximum to about 6 for CTCF and 8 for SMC1 makes the peaks easier to see.
  • In the loop track, set "Max distance (bp)" to 2000000 (2 Mb) to show the loops in this region.
  • To hide the square Hi-C map and show only the rotated map and the tracks, use Hide contact map (tracks only) under Display → Map.

You can now check how the loop anchors are positioned relative to the CTCF and SMC1 peaks.

docs.title: 5. Move with bookmarks
docs.text:
The file sample/HiCarta_demo_bookmarks_hg19.xlsx in the HiCarta folder you downloaded contains bookmarks for the demo regions and for senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) genes.

  1. Open the bookmark section of the Navigate panel, select this file with Browse… in the Load from Excel (append) field, and click Load.
  2. Click PDGFRB / CSF1R (chr5) in the list to move to that region.

A bookmark records only the genomic location. After opening a different sample, you can use the same bookmark to navigate to that region.

docs.title: 6. Export a figure
docs.text:
1. Open Print at the top of the screen and click Open print preview.
  2. Set the destination to File and the format to PDF, and choose the output folder and the file name.
  3. Make sure Also export tracks is enabled, and click Run.

In the PDF, the Hi-C map is saved as a raster image and the axes, labels and tracks as editable vector graphics. See Make a publication figure for details.

docs.title: What to read next
docs.text:
• Compare two conditions — compare the Hi-C maps of fission yeast in G2 and in mitosis from the demo catalog.
  • Data catalog — learn how to create a catalog for your own data. You can start from a copy of sample/HiCarta_catalog_template.xlsx.
  • What HiCarta can do — the list of HiCarta's features.

docs.title: How HiCarta works
docs.text: This page explains how HiCarta maintains responsive navigation with large Hi-C datasets and how it retrieves data. For the basic operations, see Usage.

docs.title: The roles of R and the browser
docs.text:
HiCarta is built using Shiny for R. On launch, R starts a local web server on your computer (http://127.0.0.1:7788), and your browser displays the user interface.

  • R — reads files, retrieves contact matrices, maps values to colors, renders tracks, and generates PDF files.
  • Web browser — displays the interface and handles interactions such as dragging and scrolling (the map is displayed with Leaflet).

Both components run on the same computer, so you do not need a separate server. Data processing takes place locally; the retrieved data are not sent to a separate server for processing.

docs.title: Tile-based rendering
docs.text:
Like a web map, HiCarta draws the map in tiles of 256 × 256 pixels.

  1. HiCarta requests only tiles in the visible area, prioritizing those near the center of the screen.
  2. For each tile, only the matching two-dimensional region is read from the .hic file. The resolution is chosen automatically from the zoom level (level of detail, LOD).
  3. Contact values are mapped to colors, and the resulting tile image is sent to the browser. Tiles far from the visible area are discarded.

All tiles share one color scale, so the colors are consistent across tiles. When a map is opened, HiCarta scans the whole map at low resolution to set the initial maximum value.

docs.title: Partial retrieval of remote files
docs.text:
HiCarta has its own readers for .hic and bigWig files, written in R. The readers use the internal file indexes to retrieve only the required byte ranges via HTTP range requests.

  • By default, .hic and bigWig files on web servers, Dropbox shared links, and Amazon S3 can be displayed without downloading the whole file.
  • Connections are reused, and previously retrieved data are cached in memory to speed up revisits to cached regions.
  • On a slow or unstable connection, setting hic_engine = download in config.txt saves the entire file to the _hic_cache/ folder first and reads it from there. The first view takes longer, but later operations may be more stable.
  • BED, GFF3, and Border Strength files are read in full when loaded. For GFF3, the parsed gene annotations are cached as *.genes.rds to accelerate subsequent loads.

docs.title: Reading private files
docs.text: For private Amazon S3 objects, whether specified as s3://bucket/key or as S3 HTTPS URLs, HiCarta signs requests using the AWS credentials stored on your computer (~/.aws/credentials). Access is determined by the permissions configured in S3. Combining object tags with per-user permissions lets you control sharing by lab or group. → Private data on Amazon S3

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text: The map origin is at the upper-left corner. Genomic coordinates increase to the right (X axis) and downward (Y axis). Tracks are drawn along the X-axis coordinates.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
HiCarta is a desktop application that runs locally on your computer. You do not need to set up a server or sign up for a HiCarta account.

On Windows, you can get started in three steps. For macOS, see the link at the end of this page.

docs.title: 1. Install R
docs.text:
Open https://cran.r-project.org and download and install R for Windows (4.1 or later). In most cases, you can accept the default installation options.

RStudio is not required

You only need to install R itself; HiCarta installs its required R packages on first launch. Having RStudio installed is also fine.

docs.title: 2. Download and unzip HiCarta
docs.text:
Open the GitHub page https://github.com/rafysta/HiCarta, then click the green "Code" button → "Download ZIP".

Right-click the downloaded ZIP file and choose "Extract All" to unzip it. You can extract it to any convenient location, such as your Desktop.

docs.title: 3. Double-click run_windows.bat
docs.text:
Inside the unzipped folder, double-click run_windows.bat.

On first launch, HiCarta automatically installs the required R packages, which may take a few minutes. Once setup is complete, HiCarta opens automatically in a browser tab (the address is http://127.0.0.1:7788).

Subsequent launches are usually faster. To quit the app, close the launcher window (Command Prompt).

You are now ready to use HiCarta. For basic operations, see Usage; for a detailed reference to the interface, see Screens & controls.

For macOS instructions, manual installation, or help with startup problems, see Setup details & troubleshooting.

docs.title: Screens & controls
docs.text:
This page describes HiCarta’s menus, controls, and settings. For a task-oriented introduction, see Usage instead.

The top of the screen has these menus: Data · Navigate · Display · Print · Setting · About. The Data button opens the data loading dialog; the other menus switch the control panel on the left. The Display panel has three tabs — Map · Compare · Tracks.

The typical flow is: load the catalog → click a sample → open it → pan/zoom → add tracks.

docs.title: Data (loader)
docs.text: Click the Data button at the top to open the data loading dialog. It has three tabs: Data browser / Direct file / Session.

docs.title: Data browser tab
docs.text:
The data catalog is an Excel file with one row per sample, from which you can open contact maps and tracks. To open a file without a catalog, use the Direct file tab.

Load the catalog — The path/URL field is prefilled with catalog_url from config.txt; use Browse… to select a local file (the location list starts with your favorite folders (★), then Desktop / Documents / Downloads / Home and the drives; on Windows the dialog also recognizes a Desktop folder redirected to OneDrive). Click Load catalog to load or reload the catalog. Invalid rows are excluded and reported with the sample name and the reason.

Filter and search — The left sidebar has a search-as-you-type field for sample names, a search across all columns (including comments), dropdown filters generated from the catalog columns, and a date-range filter. Filters are combined using AND logic; each dropdown lists only values consistent with the other active filters.

The sample list — Use Columns to select the displayed columns and the adjacent control to set the number of rows per page. Click a row to open the detail view, which shows all sample metadata and actions available for its file type:

  • Open as contact map — hic rows. A row holding several ;-separated .hic entries can be opened as one virtual multi-resolution dataset (“auto”) or as a single entry.
  • Open as comparison (B) — load a second map to compare (Display → Compare).
  • Add as track — track rows (bigwig / bed / gff3 / bs). A dialog allows you to set the label, color (visual palette), and height before adding the track. The catalog’s set_* columns supply the initial values.
  • Open in IGV — track rows; sends the file and the current region to a running instance of IGV Desktop (details).

set_norm, set_vmax, set_resolution from the catalog are applied when a map is opened; if set_norm is unspecified, HiCarta selects the first available normalization in the order ICE → KR → Raw.

docs.title: Direct file tab
docs.text:
Open a file without a catalog by entering its path or URL. Catalog set_* defaults (normalization, scale maximum, resolution, color, height) do not apply here — set them afterward in Display.

Contact map (.hic) — Type a path or URL (use Browse… to select a local file), optionally choose a normalization and a display name, then click Open as contact map or Open as comparison (B). Several single-resolution files can be opened together as one virtual multi-resolution dataset by separating their paths with ; (comparison B always uses one file — the first path).

Track — Type a path or URL, pick the Type (Auto detects bigWig / BED / gene (GFF3) / Border Strength from the extension), set label, color and height, then click Add track.

Data opened this way can also be saved to a session. As with data opened from the catalog, a bookmark records only the genomic position.

docs.title: Session tab
docs.text:
Save the current view to a file and restore it later.

Save current view — Downloads the view state — data source, region, color scale and all tracks — as a .json file (named HiCarta_session_<datetime>.json).

Restore from file (.json) — Type the path or URL of a saved .json (use Browse… to select a local file) and click Load to restore the saved view.

docs.title: Navigate
docs.text:
Specify the chromosome and region to display, and move around the map.

Chromosome (X axis) — Choose the chromosome to display. Chromosome names correspond to those stored in the .hic file (e.g. I / II / III for S. pombe). Choosing a different chromosome reopens the map automatically. Both chromosome lists are populated from the file each time a map is opened.

X-axis start / X-axis end (bp) — Specify the range to display, in bp.

All chromosomes (whole genome) — Select the first entry in the X-axis chromosome list. Both axes display all chromosomes end to end, allowing all chromosome pairs to be viewed at once. Cis contacts occupy the diagonal blocks, and trans contacts occupy the off-diagonal blocks. Both rulers display chromosome names, with thin lines marking chromosome boundaries. The cursor readout identifies the chromosome and the position within it. Panning, zooming, the color scale, bookmarks, comparison and export all work as usual. Tracks are hidden while this view is open, because tracks follow the coordinates of a single chromosome. They reappear when you select a single chromosome.

Chromosome (Y axis) — With same as X (normal map) selected, the map displays intra-chromosomal contacts. Choosing a different chromosome draws the inter-chromosome (trans) map between the two: the horizontal axis represents the X chromosome and the vertical axis represents the selected Y chromosome, so the map may be rectangular rather than square. A badge in the top-left corner names each axis. Tracks always follow the horizontal axis, so they remain aligned with the X-axis coordinates.

Y-axis start / Y-axis end (bp) — The vertical range, shown only when the two axes differ. Selecting a Y chromosome sets the range to its full length.

Two things work differently on an inter-chromosome map, because it lacks the symmetry of an intra-chromosomal map: the Split comparison mode is not offered (use Curtain or Difference instead), and the cursor readout omits genomic distance between the two loci.

Go to region — Jump to the chromosome/range you entered.

Pan view (direction pad) — The eight directional buttons (up/down/left/right plus diagonals) move the region in view. Up/down move along the Y axis, left/right along the X axis. The center ⌂ (home) button returns to the whole-chromosome view of that chromosome.

Step — Choose the amount each direction button moves, as a fraction of the range in view (¼ · ½ · 1).

Bookmarks — Save a region of interest and return to it with one click. Enter a name in the name field (optional) and save it with ★ Bookmark this view. A bookmark records only the genomic location — the chromosome and the X / Y ranges — with no data reference and no display settings. Clicking one moves to that region in the currently open dataset, allowing the same bookmark to be reused across samples. The current normalization, resolution, and color scale remain unchanged. Delete removes one. Bookmarks are also saved in a session, and can be exchanged as Excel files: Save to Excel downloads the list, Load from Excel (append) takes a path or URL (use Browse… to select a local file) and, on Load, appends the rows of that file (details).

docs.title: Display
docs.text:
The Map tab adjusts the open map; Compare contains the two-sample comparison controls, including the option to remove a comparison; Tracks is described below.

Adjust the color scale. All tiles use a single absolute-value color scale, ensuring consistent colors across tile boundaries.

Normalization — Switch the normalization of the open map (e.g. ICE / KR / Raw) without reopening it; the choices are what the .hic file actually contains. For a virtual multi-file dataset (“auto”), only normalizations present in every file are offered.

Resolution — Use the slider to fix the bin size, or select Auto to adjust the resolution with the zoom level. Only resolutions available for the current chromosome and normalization are offered — a .hic header lists the resolutions the file was built with, but a chromosome's matrix can carry fewer zoom levels, and a normalization vector can be missing at some of them. Zooming can therefore stop at a coarser bin size on one chromosome (or one normalization) than on another. This reflects the available data rather than a fixed resolution limit of the viewer.

Palette — Choose the color scheme (4 options: matlab, gentle, red, blue).

Max value — Dragging this slider changes the contrast and redraws all tiles. The initial value is estimated automatically by coarsely scanning the whole map when it is opened.

linear / log10(value) — Switch between linear and logarithmic scaling. The minimum is fixed at 0.

docs.title: Tracks (Display → Tracks)
docs.text:
Display 1D tracks below the contact map. Tracks remain synchronized with horizontal panning and zooming and render data for the visible genomic range. Multiple tracks can be stacked, each with its own color and height. A cursor guideline runs through the tracks.

To add a track from the catalog, click a track row in the Data browser and choose Add as track. A dialog lets you set the label, the color (visual palette) and the height before the track is added; the catalog’s set_color and set_height values are prefilled. To add a track by its path or URL, use the Direct file tab.

The Display → Tracks panel lists the added tracks as chips. Drag a chip to reorder the tracks (the display order updates accordingly). Click a chip to edit that track — label, color, height, maximum value, aggregation, per-track resolution — or delete it.

Tracks also work without a contact map: the chromosome axis is read from the first track file, a coordinate ruler is drawn on top, and you can zoom by dragging a range on the ruler.

Track types you can use:

Type What is drawn Notes bigWig Filled area By default, only the visible range is read (remote files are not downloaded in full) BED Interval boxes The whole file is read (rtracklayer) gene (GFF3) Gene arrows, exons, names + strand on top / − strand on bottom. Exons appear when zoomed in. Gene labels are selectively displayed to avoid overlap. Cached as <gff3>.genes.rds Border Strength Area of BS.norm Positive = red, negative = blue, baseline 0. Dashed lines at boundaries

For the details of each format, see Data formats; for the catalog columns that describe tracks, see Data catalog.

docs.title: Print
docs.text:
Export a selected region of the current map and tracks as a PNG image or PDF, or send it to a printer.

Click Open print preview to open the preview. There you can set:

  • Destination — Printer, or File.
  • Output folder / File name / Format — The save location and file name for file output, and the format (Image (PNG) or PDF).
  • Paper size — A4 portrait, A4 landscape, Square, or Custom (specify width/height in mm).
  • Output region — Chromosome, start and end (bp) for each axis. Leaving Chromosome (Y axis) at same as X exports the usual square map; choosing a different one exports the inter-chromosome map between the two.
  • Resolution — With same as the map on screen selected, the export uses the same bin size as the current view, including any fixed resolution selected in Display → Map. Choosing a resolution here overrides that; the line under the preview always names the resolution actually used.
  • Same bp scale on both axes — On (the default), each base pair occupies the same distance on the horizontal and vertical axes, preserving the genomic aspect ratio. The map is centered in the available space. When disabled, the map is stretched to fill the available area. Tracks stay aligned with the map either way. For an inter-chromosome map, pick a paper size close to the shape of the region to avoid a large blank margin.
  • Include coordinate ticks / Include legend / No margins — Toggle the elements included in the output.
  • Also export tracks — Export the tracks in view together.

After configuring the output, click Run.

docs.title: Setting
docs.text:
Adjust the layout and the app's defaults.

Contact map height (px) — Specify the map height. Apply it with Apply.

Fit to window — Set the map height to "window height − total track height".

Track resolution (view divisions) / Auto adjust — Adjust the drawing resolution and height of tracks.

Aggregation (whole-chromosome view) — Choose the aggregation for the whole-map view: Mean (IGV default) or Max (keep peaks).

docs.title: Edit config file…
docs.text:
Click Edit config file… to view and edit the application’s startup defaults (config.txt).

  • Interface language — Switch between Japanese and English.
  • Default catalog (.xlsx) URL / path — The data catalog loaded by default in the Data browser.
  • Remote file reading — Stream supported remote files (default) or download them in full before loading.
  • IGV genome id — Sent along with "Open in IGV" (e.g. hg38; empty = don't send).
  • Favourite folders — Listed first, marked ★, in every Browse… dialog. One per line, name = path (or just the path). Add folder… picks one for you. Folders that do not exist are skipped.

Clicking Apply & save reloads the page and applies the settings (any map or tracks currently loaded are closed at that point).

docs.title: About
docs.text: Shows the version and author information (Hideki Tanizawa, rafysta@gmail.com).

docs.title: Operating on the map
docs.text:
Once a map is open, you can operate directly on it.

  • Drag to pan
  • Scroll to zoom (the resolution switches automatically)
  • Middle-click drag to zoom to a selected range (rubber band)

The header shows the current coordinates and resolution, and a ruler with ticks appears along the edge. Hover over the map to display the coordinates, contact value, and, where applicable, genomic distance. The origin is at the top-left, and genomic coordinates on the Y axis increase downward.

docs.title: Notes and current scope
docs.text:
• HiCarta shows both cis (intra-chromosomal) and trans (inter-chromosomal) contacts. To see an inter-chromosome map, choose a different chromosome for the Y axis in the Navigate panel, or choose All chromosomes (whole genome) (Navigate).
  • Track chromosome names (e.g. chrII) are mapped to the .hic names (II) where possible.

docs.title: Plugins: create custom tracks in R
docs.text:
A plugin is an R script that adds a custom track type to HiCarta. Typically, you define two functions: one to read data for the visible genomic region and one to render those data. HiCarta integrates the plugin with the data catalog, the "Add as track" button, the Tracks panel and settings dialog, session files, and print preview and export. The track uses the same X-axis range as the contact map.

Typical applications include custom scores (e.g., insulation scores, eigenvectors, or other per-bin values), plots your lab already generates in R, and visualizations derived directly from .hic files, such as the included Virtual 4C plugin.

Plugin directory

Every *.R file in the plugins/ folder next to app.R is loaded when HiCarta starts and whenever the page is reloaded. After editing a plugin, simply reload the browser tab. To use another directory, set plugin_dir in config.txt (Setting → Edit config file…). The About panel lists the loaded plugins and reports errors for files that failed to load.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Two example plugins are included in the plugins/ directory:

id (file_type) File What it draws table table_signal.R a table with chr / start / end / value columns (CSV, TSV, bedGraph), with negative values below a zero line v4c virtual4c.R a virtual 4C profile: contact frequencies between an anchor position and each visible bin, retrieved from the .hic file at a resolution appropriate for the view

To use one from the catalog, enter the plugin ID in the file_type column and the file path in path, then select the row and click Add as track:

id name path file_type set_anchor 11 insulation (Growing) s3://bucket/P/insulation_G.csv table 12 IL6 promoter contacts s3://bucket/P/IMR90_G.hic v4c 22766000

Columns named set_<parameter> specify plugin parameters (in this example, the anchor). A plugin can also register file extensions (table registers .csv and .tsv), allowing file_type to be left empty for those extensions.

To open a file without a catalog, go to Data → Direct file, select the plugin under Type, and add the file. Parameters are then set from the track's settings (click the track's name in the Tracks panel).

docs.title: Writing a plugin
docs.text:
A plugin script calls hicarta_plugin() once:

hicarta_plugin(
  id       = "csv",                       # file_type in the catalog (lowercase)
  label    = "CSV signal",                # shown in menus and on the track
  defaults = list(column = "value"),      # parameters and their defaults

  # data for [start, end] on chr (the part of the view inside the chromosome)
  read = function(path, chr, start, end, p) {
    d <- read.csv(path)
    d[d$chr == chr & d$end >= start & d$start <= end, ]
  },

  # draw it; the view is [vstart, vend] (may run past the chromosome ends)
  draw = function(d, chr, vstart, vend, style) {
    hc_canvas(vstart, vend, ylim = c(0, max(d[[style$params$column]], 1)))
    rect(d$start, 0, d$end, d[[style$params$column]], col = style$color, border = NA)
    hc_label(style$name)
  })

docs.title: hicarta_plugin() arguments
docs.text: Argument Meaning id the track type's name: 1–32 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting with a letter. Use this identifier in the catalog’s file_type column. Must not be a built-in type (hic, bigwig, bed, gff3, bs, arc). label human-readable name (menus, the track chip, the settings dialog) draw required. function(d, chr, vstart, vend, style) — see below read function(path, chr, start, end, p) returning data in a form accepted by draw; NULL if the plugin needs no data defaults named list of parameters with their default values. Their types determine how values entered in the catalog or dialog are converted (number, TRUE/FALSE, text) accepts the kind of file the plugin reads: "hic", "bigwig", "bed", "gff3", "bs", "arc" or "any" (default). Used to find chromosome lengths when the track is added before any contact map extensions file extensions registered by the plugin (e.g. c("csv", "tsv")), so file_type can be left empty for them chroms optional function(path) returning a named numeric vector of chromosome lengths (track-only mode) height, color defaults for a newly added track (px; any R color) description one line shown in the settings dialog

docs.title: The read() function
docs.text: read(path, chr, start, end, p) is called with the portion of the view within the chromosome boundaries and the merged parameters p (defaults, overridden by the catalog's set_ columns / the dialog / the session). The result is cached by region and parameter set, reducing repeated calls for cached views. It may return any suitable R object, such as a data frame, a matrix, or a list.

docs.title: The draw() function
docs.text:
draw(d, chr, vstart, vend, style) receives the data d returned by read() (or NULL) and must draw into the current panel with base graphics. To keep the track aligned with the map, the X-axis range must be exactly [vstart, vend]. Use hc_canvas() to set this range; do not call par(mar=).

style is a list:

Field Meaning name, color, height the track's label, color and height, as set by the user params the merged parameters (same as p in read()) ymin, ymax the Min / Max typed in the settings dialog, or NA for automatic print TRUE when drawing the print preview / export (a conventional left-hand Y axis is useful for exported figures) chrlen, dstart, dend chromosome length and the data range constrained to the chromosome boundaries path, id the file and the plugin id

docs.title: Helpers
docs.text:
Drawing:

Helper What it does hc_canvas(vstart, vend, ylim = c(0, 1), headroom = 0.05) initializes the panel with the correct X-axis range (5% headroom above ylim, room below zero when ylim[1] < 0) hc_label(name) the track name at the top-left, like the built-in tracks hc_guide(y) a thin guideline with its value at the right (the "inline" scale of the built-in tracks) hc_yaxis() a conventional left-hand Y axis for print and export hc_message(text) a message inside the panel ("nothing in view", an error…)

Data retrieval through HiCarta’s built-in readers (supports local files, HTTP(S) URLs, and private s3:// objects; by default, supported remote files are read without downloading them in full):

Helper What it returns hc_hic_region(path, chr, start, end, resolution, norm, chr2, start2, end2) contact matrix of [start,end] on chr (rows) against [start2,end2] on chr2 (columns); chr2 defaults to chr, the second range to the first hc_bin_starts(m, 1) / hc_bin_starts(m, 2) bin start coordinates (bp) of the rows / columns of such a matrix hc_hic_pick_resolution(path, chr, start, end, target_bins = 500, norm) the resolution in the file closest to target_bins bins across the view hc_hic_chroms(path), hc_hic_resolutions(path), hc_hic_norms(path) available chromosomes, resolutions, and normalizations in the .hic file hc_bigwig_bins(path, chr, start, end, nbins, type = "mean") a bigWig as one value per bin (type = "mean" or "max") hc_bigwig_intervals(path, chr, start, end) the raw bigWig intervals as data.frame(start, end, value)

For reading and processing data, you can use any R functions and your own R packages. Use base R graphics for rendering (e.g., rect(), lines(), and polygon()). Support for ggplot2 and other grid-based graphics in plugins is planned. Keep read() efficient: it runs when the requested region and parameter set are not cached.

docs.title: Parameters: catalog, dialog, session
docs.text:
• Catalog: a column set_<name> per parameter (set_anchor, set_norm…). Empty = the default. The usual set_color / set_height work as well.
  • Settings dialog: one text box per parameter. Empty = the default.
  • Session file: parameters are saved with the track and restored with it.
  • Min / Max in the dialog arrive as style$ymin / style$ymax; it is up to the plugin to honor them (both included plugins do).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• A plugin that fails to load is reported once when HiCarta starts and in the About panel, along with the error message. Other plugins can still load.
  • A rendering error is displayed inside the track's panel (and in the R console); the rest of the app is unaffected.
  • The track is empty: check that read() filters on the chromosome name the contact map uses (chr1 vs 1), and that the file's coordinates are in bp.
  • Edited the plugin and nothing changed? Reload the browser page.

Plugins are code

A plugin is ordinary R code and runs with the same rights as HiCarta itself. Only place trusted scripts in the plugin directory.

docs.title: Setup details & troubleshooting
docs.text: This page provides detailed setup instructions and troubleshooting guidance if the steps in Installation do not work for you.

docs.title: Get it with Git (instead of the ZIP)
docs.text:
If Git is installed, you can clone the repository instead of downloading the ZIP file. This makes it easier to retrieve future updates.

git clone https://github.com/rafysta/HiCarta.git

docs.title: Start it on macOS
docs.text:
Follow these steps to start HiCarta on macOS.

  1. Install R (4.1 or later) from https://cran.r-project.org (the CRAN .pkg, or brew install --cask r).

  2. Download and unzip HiCarta.

  3. Double-click run_mac.command in the folder.

If macOS blocks the launcher with a message such as "cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified", try right-click run_mac.command → "Open". If the file lacks execute permission, run the following command once in the terminal from the HiCarta directory:

chmod +x run_mac.command

To stop the app, press Ctrl+C in the terminal window or close the window.

docs.title: Required R packages
docs.text:
On first launch, the launcher checks for missing packages and, if needed, runs R/install_libraries.R to install them automatically. The packages and their purposes are listed below:

Package Source Purpose shiny, leaflet, htmlwidgets, base64enc CRAN Application interface and tile-based map display data.table CRAN Fast text-file parsing RColorBrewer CRAN Color palettes jsonlite CRAN Saving/restoring sessions shinyFiles CRAN The "Browse…" dialog for local files curl CRAN HTTP range requests for remote .hic and bigWig strawr CRAN Optional. Fallback .hic reader; not normally required rtracklayer Bioconductor BED tracks (bigWig is read by the built-in reader)

Installing rtracklayer

rtracklayer comes from Bioconductor, so the initial installation can take a few minutes. This is normal.

To install the required packages manually, start R with the HiCarta folder as the working directory and run:

source("R/install_libraries.R")

docs.title: How starting and stopping works
docs.text: HiCarta starts a local web server and opens a browser tab at http://127.0.0.1:7788. To stop it, on Windows close the launcher window (Command Prompt), and on macOS press Ctrl+C in the terminal or close the window. If port 7788 is already in use, the launcher automatically terminates the previous instance before starting.

docs.title: "Could not find Rscript" appears
docs.text: R may not be installed, or Rscript may not be available on your PATH. Install R if necessary and relaunch HiCarta. On Windows the launcher also searches C:\Program Files\R\.

docs.title: rtracklayer fails to install
docs.text:
Ensure that you have an internet connection on first launch. If installation still fails, start R and install it directly:

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("rtracklayer")

docs.title: Nothing shows / the map is blank
docs.text: Check that a dataset is loaded in Data and that a valid region is selected in Navigate, then click Open map.

docs.title: A remote .hic or track feels slow
docs.text:
By default, remote .hic files are streamed: HiCarta retrieves only the required data via HTTP range requests and reuses the connection. The .hic file is not saved to disk as a whole. Cached data are retrieved from memory rather than fetched again.

If your connection is slow or unreliable, downloading the entire file first may improve subsequent navigation. Change the mode via Setting → Edit config file… → Remote file reading, or configure it manually in config.txt:

hic_engine = download     # fetch the whole file into _hic_cache/ first
hic_engine = native       # stream (default)

This setting also applies to bigWig tracks. rtracklayer may fail to open a remote bigWig (Couldn't open ... UCSC library operation failed), so HiCarta reads them with its own streaming reader. Remote BED, GFF3, and Border Strength files are downloaded and parsed in full, regardless of this setting.

In download mode, files are saved in _hic_cache/. To free space, quit the app and delete that folder (files are fetched again when needed).

There is a third value, strawr, which uses the legacy strawr reader. It is intended for diagnostic use only and can be very slow for remote URLs — strawr::readHicNormTypes() has no HTTP code path, so each call takes a long time and may not return the full list of normalizations.

docs.title: Change the startup defaults (config.txt)
docs.text: Defaults such as the catalog URL, remote-file reading mode, IGV genome ID, interface language and the AWS profile for private S3 data are saved in config.txt in the same folder as the app. You can edit them from Setting → Edit config file… in HiCarta (see Screens & controls for details). To edit it manually, copy config.example.txt to config.txt and edit it.

docs.title: Tutorial: compare two conditions
docs.text: This tutorial explains how to compare two Hi-C maps in a single view, using fission yeast Hi-C data from G2 phase and mitosis in the demo data (Tanizawa et al., Nat Struct Mol Biol 2017). The data were collected from synchronized cdc25-22 cells, 20 minutes (G2) and 50 minutes (mitosis) after release from the cell-cycle block.

docs.title: 1. Open sample A
docs.text:
1. Open Data and load the demo catalog (see First 5 minutes).
  2. Click the row S. pombe Hi-C G2 (cdc25, 20 min) and click Open as contact map. This is sample A.
  3. In the Navigate panel, choose chromosome II (II).

docs.title: 2. Open sample B
docs.text:
1. Go back to Data, click the row S. pombe Hi-C mitosis (cdc25, 50 min) and click Open as comparison (B).
  2. The message "Comparison ready" shows the common resolutions and the sequencing-depth correction factor.

The two files must meet the following requirements for comparison. If they are incompatible, HiCarta displays the reason.

  • The same genome (the same chromosome names and lengths)
  • At least one common resolution
  • The normalization selected for sample A (KR, for example) must also be available in sample B. Both samples are read with the same normalization.

docs.title: 3. Choose a view mode
docs.text: Select a comparison mode under View mode in Display → Compare.

docs.title: Split
docs.text:
Shows sample A in the upper right and sample B in the lower left of the diagonal. An intra-chromosomal Hi-C map is symmetric about the diagonal, so the two triangular halves allow both samples to be compared within one map. Enable Draw a line along the diagonal to mark the boundary.

In this example, the mitotic map (lower left) shows a broader band of contact enrichment along the diagonal and more prominent large domains than the G2 map (upper right). Condensin has been reported to mediate the formation of large domains of approximately 300 kb to 1 Mb during mitosis.

docs.title: Curtain
docs.text: Drag the divider to switch between the samples on its two sides. The spacebar (or the Switch A / B button) switches the whole map between A and B instantly. Alternating between samples at the same genomic region makes small differences easier to notice. Esc returns to the divider view.

docs.title: Difference
docs.text:
Displays differences between the maps using a symmetric color scale centered on zero. Positive and negative values share the same scale, and values beyond the selected limits are displayed using the endpoint colors.

Setting What it does Formula log2 fold change log2((A+ε)/(B+ε)) or difference A − B Pseudo-count ε Reduces extreme ratios in bins with few contacts and prevents division by zero. Increasing the pseudocount can reduce visual noise, but may also attenuate fold changes. Scale limit The magnitude at which the color scale saturates (± log2 or ± counts) Diverging palette blue − white − red, or blue − white − orange and purple − white − green, which are designed to accommodate color vision deficiencies

The default pseudocount and scale limit are computed from the whole chromosome when sample B is loaded.

docs.title: 4. Sequencing-depth correction
docs.text:
Samples with different sequencing depths can differ in overall signal intensity. When Correct for sequencing depth automatically is on, HiCarta multiplies the values of sample B by the ratio of total contact counts (A / B). You can also set the factor manually in Factor applied to B.

When interpreting a difference map, consider differences in sequencing depth and check whether correction is enabled. This correction is based on total contact counts and does not constitute a statistical significance test.

docs.title: 5. Things to keep in mind
docs.text:
• Resolution — at high resolution, individual matrix bins tend to contain fewer contacts, which can increase noise in the difference map. Assess broad differences at a coarser resolution, then inspect details using the split or curtain view. You can fix the resolution under Display → Map.
  • Color scale — the split and curtain views use the same color scale for A and B.
  • Interchromosomal maps — an inter-chromosomal map has no symmetry diagonal, so the split view is not available. Use the curtain or difference view.
  • Cursor — hovering over the map shows the values of A and B for that matrix bin, log2(A/B) and A − B.

docs.title: 6. Export the comparison as a figure
docs.text:
Export the current comparison view using Print → Open print preview. With Sample info under the map on, a split-view figure includes information for sample A (upper right) and sample B (lower left). See Make a publication figure for export details.

To stop comparing, click Remove comparison in Display → Compare.

docs.title: Tutorial: make a publication figure
docs.text:
This tutorial explains how to export the displayed Hi-C map and tracks as a PDF figure for publication and refine the figure in Illustrator, Inkscape, or similar tools.

In the PDF, the Hi-C map is saved as a raster image, and the coordinate ticks, labels, legend, and tracks as editable vector graphics. Rasterizing the map helps keep file sizes manageable, even at high resolution, while allowing text and lines to be edited afterward.

docs.title: 1. Set up the figure on screen
docs.text:
The figure is generated from the current view. Configure the displayed data first to minimize adjustments in the print preview.

  • Region — navigate to the genomic region you want to export. Exact coordinates can also be entered in the preview.
  • Colors — choose the palette and the maximum value under Display → Map.
  • Tracks — add the tracks you need, and configure their order, names, colors, heights, and maximum values under Display → Tracks. Track names become the labels in the figure.
  • Comparison — for a figure comparing two conditions, switch to a comparison view first (Compare two conditions).

docs.title: 2. Open the print preview
docs.text:
Open Print at the top of the screen and click Open print preview. The preview updates when you change a setting.

Setting What it does Destination File or Printer Output folder / File name / Format The format is PDF or Image (PNG). PDF is recommended for editable publication figures. Paper size A4 portrait, A4 landscape, square or custom (width and height in mm) Output region Chromosome, start and end (bp) on each axis. Choosing a different chromosome for the Y axis exports an inter-chromosome map. Resolution Select "same as the map on screen" to use the resolution of the current view. The resolution actually used is shown below the preview. Same bp scale on both axes Uses the same scale per base pair along both axes (enabled by default), preserving the genomic aspect ratio. Include coordinate ticks / Include legend Whether to include the coordinate ticks and the color-scale legend No margins Exports only the map, without margins. Use this option if you plan to recreate the axes and labels manually. Sample info under the map Includes the sample name, genomic region, and resolution below the figure. For split-view comparisons, information for sample A (upper right) and sample B (lower left) is also included. Also export tracks Exports the visible tracks together with the map, aligned horizontally with it.

docs.title: 3. Export
docs.text: After configuring the output, click Run. A message displays the saved file location. The preview stays open, so you can change the region or settings and export again.

docs.title: 4. Finish in Illustrator or Inkscape
docs.text:
Open the exported PDF in Illustrator or Inkscape, and select and edit individual coordinate ticks, labels, legends, and track lines and fills.

  • Change fonts, font sizes, line widths and colors to meet the journal's requirements.
  • The Hi-C map is a raster image. Scale the map and the tracks together to keep their positions aligned.
  • When arranging figures from multiple genomic regions or conditions side by side, export them with the same settings (paper size, resolution, maximum value) to keep their sizes and color scales consistent.

For slides and posters

Set the format to Image (PNG) to export an image that can be inserted directly into a slide or poster.

docs.title: 5. Recreate the same figure later
docs.text: If you save a session, you can restore the view later, including the data sources, region, color scale and tracks. This is useful when you need to recreate or revise a figure during peer review. → Save the view and reproduce it later (session)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
This guide covers common tasks in HiCarta. For detailed explanations of individual controls and settings, see Screens & controls, linked from each item.

The basic flow is: load data → open the map → move and zoom.

docs.title: Loading data
docs.text: Data can be loaded from the data catalog — an Excel file with one row per sample. Click the Data button at the top of the screen to open the data loading dialog. It has three tabs (Data browser, Direct file and Session), and you can also enter the path or URL of a file directly.

docs.title: Load a Hi-C map
docs.text:
1. Click the Data button at the top.
  2. On the Data browser tab, load your catalog (click Load catalog; the field is prefilled from config.txt; use Browse… to select a local .xlsx file).
  3. Use the sidebar filters or search to find the desired sample, and click the sample's row.
  4. In the detail view, click Open as contact map.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Data, Data catalog

docs.title: Load a bigWig
docs.text:
1. In the Data browser, click the row of a bigWig sample.
  2. Click Add as track, adjust the label, color, and height in the dialog, and confirm.

If a Hi-C map is already open, the track is aligned with the genomic coordinates of the map.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Tracks

docs.title: Tracks without a contact map
docs.text:
You can add tracks without opening a Hi-C map. HiCarta then reads the chromosome names and lengths from the first track file you add and displays the full length of the first chromosome; the contact map stays hidden.

  • Chromosome lengths are obtained from the bigWig header or estimated from the maximum coordinate in a BED / GFF3 / *_BS.txt file.
  • Navigate from the Navigate panel: select a chromosome to display its full length, enter the start and end coordinates, and click Go to region, pan with the left/right buttons, and zoom with + / −.
  • If the file contains no usable chromosome information, HiCarta displays a message. In that case, open a Hi-C map first.
  • If you subsequently open a Hi-C map, the contact map appears and is synchronized with the tracks.
  • Print also supports track-only views (a coordinate axis plus the tracks).

docs.title: Load Border Strength / genes / BED
docs.text:
As with other tracks, register the file in the catalog (set file_type to bs, gff3, or bed, or let HiCarta infer the type from the extension), click the row in the Data browser, and choose Add as track.

Border Strength (*_BS.txt): positive values are drawn in red, negative values in blue, and boundaries are marked with dashed lines. For the file formats, see Data formats.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Tracks

docs.title: Navigating the displayed region
docs.text: Navigation controls are available in the Navigate panel on the left of the screen.

docs.title: Move to any location
docs.text:
1. Choose Navigate in the top menu.
  2. Choose a Chromosome (X axis), and enter the range you want in X-axis start and X-axis end (bp). For an inter-chromosome map, also set the Y-axis chromosome and range.
  3. Click Go to region.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Navigate

docs.title: Move with buttons
docs.text:
Use the direction pad in the Navigate menu (up/down/left/right plus diagonals) to move the map. Set the movement per click using Step (¼ · ½ · 1 screen). You can also drag the map to pan or scroll to zoom.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Navigate

docs.title: Show the whole chromosome
docs.text:
Click the button in the center of the direction pad (⌂) in the Navigate menu to return to the whole-chromosome view.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Navigate

docs.title: Bookmark a region of interest
docs.text:
1. Display the region you want to bookmark.
  2. Optionally, enter a bookmark name in the field at the bottom of the Navigate panel.
  3. Click ★ Bookmark this view.

Saved bookmarks appear in a list. Click a bookmark to return to the corresponding genomic region. Bookmarks record only genomic locations, allowing you to revisit the same region across samples. The current normalization, resolution, and color scale remain unchanged. To remove an unwanted bookmark, use Delete. Save to Excel / Load from Excel (append) allow you to export or import the bookmark list as an .xlsx file that you can annotate and share (details).

→ Details: Screens & controls - Navigate

docs.title: Change the contrast (color intensity)
docs.text:
Choose Display in the top menu and drag the Max value slider to change the contrast. Switching between linear / log10 and choosing a Palette are also done here.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Display

docs.title: Adjust map height and layout
docs.text:
In Setting in the top menu, you can set the Contact map height, adjust the map to fit the available window height with Fit to window, and adjust track heights and resolution.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Setting

docs.title: Save the view and reproduce it later (session)
docs.text:
To save:

  1. Open the Data button → Session tab.
  2. Click Save current view to download a .json file.

To restore:

  1. Open the Data button → Session tab.
  2. In Restore from file (.json), select the saved .json file and click Load.

The data sources, genomic region, color scale, tracks, and other saved settings are restored together. The original data files must still be accessible.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Data (Session)

docs.title: Export a figure / print
docs.text:
1. Open the map you want to export.
  2. Choose Print in the top menu and click Open print preview.
  3. In the preview, set the destination (Printer / File), format (PNG / PDF), paper size, output region, whether to include coordinate ticks, the legend and margins, and whether to include tracks.
  4. Click Run.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Print

docs.title: Switch the display language
docs.text:
Open Setting → Edit config file… in the top menu, choose the Interface language, and click Apply & save. The page reloads and the language switches. Because changing the language closes the currently open map and tracks, use the session save feature if you want to return to the same state.

→ Details: Screens & controls - Setting

docs.title: HiCarta
docs.text:
Hi-C マップを、地図アプリのように。

HiCarta は、Hi-C データを可視化する無料のデスクトップアプリです。複数の染色体を俯瞰する全ゲノム表示から個々の遺伝子のスケールまで、ドラッグとスクロールで自由に移動・拡大・縮小できます。ループや ChIP-seq などのトラックの同時表示、異なる条件の Hi-C マップの比較、R による独自の描画機能の追加、論文用の編集可能な図の出力にも対応しています。

お使いの PC 上で動作し、専用サーバーの構築は不要です。R をインストールしておけば、ダブルクリックで起動できます。名前の「Carta」は、イタリア語やラテン語で「地図・海図」を意味します。

4 分のデモ動画です（1 分の紹介 もあります）。

docs.title: 可視化の例
docs.text:
Hi-C マップ 2 条件の比較（右上と左下に分割表示） 回転マップ＋ループ＋ChIP-seq ChIP-seq トラック＋遺伝子 R によるカスタムトラック 複数の染色体を同時表示

上の図はすべて HiCarta から PDF として出力したものです。各機能の説明は できること を参照してください。

docs.title: 目的から探す
docs.text:
• はじめての 5 分 — 公開データを使って、マップの表示からトラックの追加、図の出力までを試す
  • インストール — Windows・macOS でのインストールと起動
  • 2 つの条件を比較する — 対角分割・カーテン・差分マップの 3 種類の比較表示
  • 論文用の図を作る — 印刷プレビューから PDF を出力し、Illustrator などで仕上げる
  • 自分のデータを使う — Excel のデータカタログの書き方
  • 未発表データを共有する — Amazon S3 のアクセス制御を使う
  • 独自のトラックを作る — R のプラグイン
  • 他のツールとの比較 — Juicebox、HiGlass、JBrowse 2 などとの違い

docs.title: 既存のデータファイルをそのまま利用する
docs.text: .hic ファイルや各種トラックのデータを、ローカルの PC、Web サーバー、Dropbox の共有リンク、Amazon S3（公開・非公開）から開けます。リモートの .hic や bigWig は必要な部分だけを読み込むため、事前にファイル全体をダウンロードする必要はありません。仕組みは HiCarta のしくみ で説明しています。

docs.title: クイックスタート
docs.text:
1. https://cran.r-project.org から R（4.1 以上）をインストールします。

  2. GitHub で Code → Download ZIP から入手し、展開します。

  3. 起動します。

    • Windows — run_windows.bat をダブルクリックします。
    • macOS — run_mac.command をダブルクリックします（起動がブロックされた場合は、右クリック → 開く）。

    初回起動時は必要な R パッケージが自動的にインストールされるため、数分かかることがあります。 4. Web ブラウザに HiCarta が表示されます。続けて はじめての 5 分 でデモデータを開いてみてください。

詳細は インストール と セットアップの詳細とトラブルシューティング を参照してください。

開発者: 谷澤英樹（Hideki Tanizawa）（rafysta@gmail.com）、北海道大学 遺伝子病制御研究所 ソース: github.com/rafysta/HiCarta · MIT ライセンス 質問・不具合報告・機能のご要望は GitHub Issues からお知らせください。

docs.title: 他のツールとの比較
docs.text: Hi-C データを表示するツールには、それぞれ異なる特徴があります。HiCarta は、研究室で保有するデータを手元の PC で手軽に閲覧・比較し、その結果を論文用の図として出力することを重視しています。公開データの閲覧や、大規模な共同研究用のデータポータルの構築には、ほかのツールの方が向いている場合もあります。

docs.title: 機能の比較
docs.text:
